key_questions.answer: Probably in range but in the lower half: about $97-99m against the $99.5m midpoint, roughly -1.5% versus the priced answer. I rebuilt it from the company's own history. Revenue per business day from FQ4 to FQ1 fell to 0.945x (FY25 to FY26) and 0.954x (FY24 to FY25). FQ4 FY26 was $106.1m over 64 business days, about $104.6m once the roughly 2 months of Sitrick are taken out (Sitrick was sold 2026-05-02 and ran at about $2.3m a quarter). FQ1 FY27 has 63 US business days. That gives $97.3-98.3m, or $99.2m if no Sitrick adjustment is made. Year on year the same answer appears: FQ1 FY26 was $120.2m ($117.9m ex Sitrick), and the current -17% trend gives about $97.9m. Two things argue the other way. The guide was set on 2026-07-22, about seven weeks into a 13-week quarter, so management saw most of the quarter. And they have landed inside their outlook for three straight quarters. Peers have also improved since RGP last spoke. All of this is inside the guided range, so the market was told to expect it.

key_questions.answer: The FQ2 guide is more likely flat to down sequentially, with a midpoint around $94-98m, than at or above $102m. RGP's own Q1-to-Q2 revenue ratio was 0.979 (FY26), 0.958 (FY24) and 1.063 (FY25), and FQ2 carries Labor Day and Thanksgiving. Management talked growth only for the 'latter half' of FY27. The stale street implies improvement: the Q2 EPS consensus of -$0.13 against -$0.22 for Q1, and FY27 revenue of $426m, which needs about $109m a quarter from Q2. But that consensus is two estimates far apart (-$0.02 vs -$0.24), with nothing revised in at least four weeks. The low one, Noble's -$0.24, assumes no improvement, which is my answer. On the other side, peers that reported after RGP improved: Robert Half talent solutions grew sequentially for a third quarter and guides Q3 +1-5% y/y; Korn Ferry fee revenue is +7%; US temp-help employment is +1.5% y/y to August. That raises the odds of a 'stabilizing' guide. Net: a modest negative, capped because the bar is disputed and the answer rests on my inference.

key_questions.answer: Margin and SG&A should land inside the guide. My arithmetic on the guide: $98m at 37.5% gives about $36.8m gross profit, against $42m run-rate SG&A, $2.5m non-run-rate costs and about $1.0m of D&A and amortization. That is an operating loss near -$8.7m, or about -$0.25 to -$0.27 GAAP EPS, a little worse than the -$0.22 consensus, whose basis is unclear. Adjusted EBITDA comes out about -$4m to -$5m, against -$0.6m in FQ4. FQ1 is seasonally a cash-use quarter: -$7.8m of operating cash flow and $86.1m falling to $77.5m in FQ1 FY26, when EBITDA was positive. With $7.7m of Sitrick/separation cash costs partly accrued and the dividend, I expect cash in the high $60m to low $70m range against $82.4m. That is not distress: there is no debt and an undrawn $30m revolver. But it sits beside a market cap of about $127m. All of it is inside the guide, so it is small.

investment_decision.reason: Q2 carries the decision. RGP's own seasonality and its 'latter half' growth language point to a flat-to-down FQ2 guide, while the street's Q2 and FY27 numbers are stale (no revision since late July) and lifted by one outlier estimate, so a guide below the street is more likely than not, as in July.
